title: Flick core: modules, event bus, control socket
Quality gates: Rust check:all (fmt, clippy pedantic subset, test, custom checks) + CI + pre-commit
description:
Port the os-eco check:all standard (~/Projects/os-eco/docs/check-all-standard.md, template ~/Projects/os-eco/templates/l5-toolkit/) to Rust.

Runner: scripts/check-all.sh with the same contract as check-all.ts: gates run in a fixed order; each prints one ✓/✗ line with its time; on failure it prints only lines matching error/warning/FAILED/panicked/budget (or the last 25 lines) plus a re-run hint; --bail; CHECK_ALL_VERBOSE=1.

Gates, in order:
1. lint: cargo fmt --check (rustfmt.toml max_width=100) + cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -D warnings. Lints go in Cargo.toml [lints]: clippy all=deny, pedantic=warn, plus unwrap_used, expect_used, panic, todo, dbg_macro, undocumented_unsafe_blocks, multiple_unsafe_ops_per_block, allow_attributes_without_reason, too_many_lines, cognitive_complexity (clippy.toml threshold 15). Relax the FFI-noisy pedantic lints. Existing violations use #[expect(..., reason)].
2. check:layers: unsafe/objc2/CF only under src/platform; src/core imports no platform; modules never import each other. Grep script, rules in scripts/layer-rules.toml, every allow entry has a why. Starts as a no-op until flick-ee5b lands.
3. check:agents: backticked paths and commands in AGENTS.md must exist (port of validate-agents-md.ts).
4. check:deps: cargo machete + cargo deny check (advisories, licenses, sources).
5. check:size: file-size ratchet, 500 lines, src/**/*.rs + tests; budgets in scripts/file-size-budgets.json; stale entries fail.
6. check:debt: TODO/FIXME/HACK/XXX must cite flick-xxxx, #N or a URL; path:line allowlist; stale entries fail.
7. check:binary-size: release binary ratchet (start at 5 MB).
8. check:coverage: cargo llvm-cov over the pure modules (core/, config, store, search) with an up-only floor in scripts/coverage-budgets.json.
9. check:ci-parity: CI runs scripts/check-all.sh only, so parity holds by construction; the script only asserts that.

Skip jscpd (it is a Node tool and the codebase is small); revisit later.
Hooks: scripts/hooks/pre-commit runs the full check-all.sh (warren policy: if a check is too slow for the hook, fix the check), with GIT_* env vars unset. Install it with scripts/setup.sh (git config core.hooksPath scripts/hooks).
Every ratchet budget only moves one way, and the scripts never edit their own budgets.

title: Create Quicklink from the launcher UI (Raycast-style form)
description:
Add/edit/delete quicklinks without hand-editing config.toml, like Raycast's 'Create Quicklink'.

- Builtin item 'Create Quicklink' opens a form view: name, URL/path (with {query} placeholder), optional keyword, optional app to open with. Tab between fields; Enter saves; Esc cancels.

- Persist by appending/updating [[quicklink.links]] in config.toml (preserve comments/formatting, e.g. toml_edit), then reload. Write the new table form, not legacy [[quicklinks]] (see flick-c3c1).
- Validate: unique name (see flick-abe2 duplicate-name bug), non-empty URL, keyword not clashing.
- Needs a form/text-field ListView kind in core + panel support; keep it generic so other modules can reuse it.
- CLI parity: flick quicklink add <name> <url> [--keyword k].

title: Rebuild / reinstall Flick from the launcher (from the local checkout)
description:
Let the user install the latest local code from inside Flick, instead of asking an agent to run scripts/bundle.sh --install.

Source of truth is the LOCAL checkout, not origin. Agents commit locally, and those commits are often ahead of GitHub. A git pull would miss that work, or conflict with it. No git network operations.

- 'Rebuild Flick': build from the checkout's current HEAD, reinstall, relaunch. 'Rebuild Flick (dirty)' or a modifier key: build the working tree as it is, uncommitted changes included, and mark the version '-dirty'.
- 'Flick Version' / launcher subtitle: installed commit + build time, and whether the checkout is ahead ('3 commits newer in ~/Projects/flick: <subjects>'). Bake the commit sha into the binary at build time.
- Checkout path: [flick] source = "~/Projects/flick" in config, defaulting to the path baked in at build time.
- Optional: on LauncherOpened/Wake, compare the installed sha to the checkout HEAD with local git only. If they differ, show a 'Rebuild available' item. Never rebuild automatically.
- Run the build on a background thread with progress in the panel ('Building… 42s'). Post the result to the main thread via the event channel. Log output to a file and open the log on failure.
- Never leave a half-installed app: build into target/, run gates or at least cargo build first, and swap the bundle only on success.
- Relaunch through a detached helper, or launchd, which bundle.sh already uses, so the old process can quit. Keep the single-instance check working across the swap.
- Optional: build a different branch or worktree, for example to try an agent's worktree before merging.
- CLI parity: flick flick rebuild [--dirty] | version.

title: KOTA cards: declarative JSON cards with dynamic actions, rendered natively, presses round-trip to KOTA or act locally
description:
Decisions (Jaymin, 2026-10-10): (1) shell actions need the in-card confirm even on locally posted cards. (2) No interpolation of field values into URLs/scripts/shell in v1. (3) Invalid card JSON is rejected with a precise reason returned to the poster (distinct exit code); KOTA retries/decides; kota-flick-say must NOT fall back to iMessage on a rejection (only on transport failure). (4) max_cards=4 and pending_timeout_secs=120 are defaults, both configurable under [message].

Spec agreed with KOTA: JSON on stdin, {v:1,id,title,reply_to?,thread?,state:open|done|error,blocks:[text{md},kv{items:[[k,v]]},list{items},progress{value,label},choice{id,options,multi},field{id,placeholder,multiline}],actions:[{id,label,style:primary|default|destructive}]}; full replace by id; unknown blocks degrade to text; ~16KB cap; after a press the card shows pending until KOTA updates it. Reply path: printf %s '<values json>' | ssh jaymin@mbp-server .dotfiles/home/.local/bin/kota-ask --action --card <id> --action-id <id> (ids [A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}, values <=4000 chars, exit 2 on bad input). Actions may also act locally: open URL, open app, run a configured script, run a flick verb, copy; arbitrary shell needs explicit confirmation showing the command. Several cards at once (stack), keyboard-reachable without stealing focus by default.

title: KOTA status item: presence (idle/thinking/down), pending-card badge, quick ask, inbox
description: Menu bar item shows KOTA presence from herdr pane status of mbp-server KOTA and kota-dash /ok (https://mbp-server.tail1b7f44.ts.net:8310), a badge for cards awaiting the user, and a menu/popover with quick ask, recent cards and fleet health summary.

title: KOTA chat window: key-capable floating panel, threads, inline cards, context attach
description: Native floating panel that takes keyboard input, opened by hotkey. Threaded transcript (kota-ask --thread), cards inline, streaming via repeated posts with the same id. Attach context: frontmost app/window, selection, clipboard, screenshot (copied to mbp-server first). Reused by local/private chat and the dashboard.

title: Local model chat on the Mac Pro, with a truly private mode (nothing stored anywhere)
description: Chat against mlx-serve/ollama on the Mac Pro over Tailscale, in the chat window. Private mode: conversation only in memory, never in flick.db or logs, cleared on close. The current mlx-serve (com.jaymin.mlx-serve, :11234, shared with mailwatch/kota-memory) logs the first ~80 chars of every user message to ~/.mlx-serve/logs/{daemon,mlx-serve-11234}.log, so private mode needs a separate instance (e.g. :11235) with --log-file off --log-level error, stdout/stderr to /dev/null, --prefix-cache-entries 0. Normal local chat may persist history.

title: Dictation anywhere: hold right_cmd+right_shift, speak, transcript pastes into the focused field (laptop-local STT)
description: Wispr Flow-style. Chord right_cmd+right_shift (hold) via the keys module; record mic while held; transcribe on the laptop (whisper.cpp is installed via brew; parakeet-mlx is an option); paste into the focused field. Audio and text never leave the laptop. Separate from KOTA push-to-talk (right_cmd+right_alt -> kota-voice :8600).

title: Fleet dashboard: sys verb on every Flick, aggregated view of MBP, mbp-server, Mac Pro and their services
description: Each Flick exposes 'sys' (cpu, mem, disk, battery, uptime, key services) over the remote transport; the laptop aggregates. Service checks: kota-dash, mlx-serve, ollama, kota-memory, mailwatch backlog, pundit, syncthing, minecraft, herdr agents. Actions: restart service, Screen Sharing (vnc://), tail log, wake. Mac Pro has no Flick yet: install it or fall back to ssh. Launcher view first, persistent window later.

title: Unprompted KOTA posts can be missed: card shows once for timeout_secs (30) and is gone; no badge or unread state
description: KOTA (2026-10-09 22:46 PT) posted mmv1z24hh7 (screen-time nudge) with no --reply-to; post succeeded and the message is in history (flick message ls), but Jaymin never saw it. Replies after a k prompt (mmv1zao368, mmv1zbm819) were seen because he was watching for them. Code path: message::post always calls display(); the HUD uses CanJoinAllSpaces|FullScreenAuxiliary at level 25 and orderFrontRegardless on the screen under the pointer, so it most likely appeared and timed out (timeout_secs = 30) while he was not looking (possibly display asleep or locked; no Locked/Idle check before showing). Nothing records unread, so the miss is silent. Fix direction: unread state per message; do not start the timeout while locked/display asleep/idle (show on Unlocked/Active instead); unsolicited posts stay until dismissed or go to an inbox with a menu-bar badge (fold into flick-4354 inbox and flick-7da1 stack, e.g. a per-post --sticky or default sticky when no reply_to). title: remote: accept phone app-open events from flick-ios so KOTA can read them
description:
flick-ios (../flick-ios) sends one event per app open over the remote TCP protocol (JSON argv line, port 7419). Peer = the iPhone's Tailscale machine name in [remote] peers. Goal: KOTA sees phone usage through Flick, before any blocking.

Event: client event id, device, app (bundle id or name), opened_at. Later (prompt): reason, minutes granted.
- New verb (e.g. `activity phone add ...`) allowed by net_policy for remote callers; idempotent on the event id so the phone can retry its queue.
- Storage: new table, not a column on activity_spans. Released migrations are permanent; leave room for reason/minutes.
- Read side: `flick activity today|spans` (and --json) include phone opens next to Mac spans, under the existing remote grant, so KOTA reads them like Mac activity.
- Receiver: the Mac Pro, Tailscale name jaymins-mac-pro (decided 2026-10-10). Always on and on the phone's Apple ID, so it also gets Biome Screen Time (flick-473f). KOTA reads it with `flick --host jaymins-mac-pro activity ... --remote` (mbp-server in its [remote] peers, `flick activity remote allow` there). The laptop's Mac spans stay in the laptop's flick.db; a merged report across Macs is a later seed.
- Update docs/remote.md, docs/activity.md, ARCHITECTURE.md.

Spike. With Screen Time 'Share across devices', macOS syncs iPhone usage into Biome (~/Library/Biome/streams/...). Reading it gives per-app durations without the phone app; it complements flick-ios's open events. Needs Full Disk Access; undocumented, changes between macOS versions. First: find the stream and decode one day of rows on this Mac.
